channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: The Hand Magazine - Issue #54 Autumn 2026
item.description: Submit up to 5 images for Issue #54 of this international publication focused on photographic printmaking and hand-printed work. No theme — variety wanted. Must be a subscriber to submit. Ideal for alternative process artists. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $15–$30. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Traces — Volume 01 · The Slow Archive
item.description: Open call for the first digital publication of The Slow Archive, a platform for slow landscape photography. The theme 'Traces' invites reflection on signs of presence — a mark, a structure, a path, a subtle intervention, human or not, visible or almost invisible — within the landscape. The call seeks quiet images that suggest rather than explain. Selected works are featured in the platform's debut digital volume. Open to established artists and emerging photographers from any country. — Deadline: July 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: On the Shelf 2026 · Filter Photo
item.description: Juried photo book exhibition at Filter Space, Filter Photo's Chicago gallery, juried by Nick Larsen of Radius Books. All types of photo books are welcome — self-published, handmade, or commercially published — including multi-artist titles, provided the book was completed within the last three years. Selected books are exhibited at Filter Space September 4 – October 31, 2026, with a gallery reception on September 25. One Juror's Choice winner receives a $500 cash prize, with an additional Honorable Mention. Accepted artists are responsible for shipping their books to and from the gallery. — Deadline: July 15, 2026. Fee: $25 (1 book). Prize: $500 Juror's Choice.

item.title: The Salon — London Photo Show 2026
item.description: Open call for The Salon, a juried group exhibition at Hoxton Arches in London, June 24–28 2026. Selected images are professionally printed (8×6") and displayed with the photographer's name in the gallery. Open to all photographers, whether or not they have exhibited before. Standout entries receive partner prizes from Think Tank, 36exp and Point 101, including a large-format archival Hahnemühle print. Submit 1, 3 or 5 images (£35 / £75 / £100). — Deadline: June 17, 2026. Fee: £35 (1 image). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Paris Photo Students Prize 2026
item.description: Annual prize supporting photography and visual arts students from European schools. A jury of art professionals selects 20 students from roughly 600 applications, and four laureates are chosen. Laureates present their projects in a dedicated space at Paris Photo (Grand Palais, November 12–15, 2026) and in an exhibition at the Gare de Lyon train station. All selected students join a professional support program, with partner awards including a FUTURES residency and grants from La Saif. — Deadline: June 8, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SlowExposures 2026 — Pop-Up Tour
item.description: Open call for the PopUp Tour at the SlowExposures festival, celebrating photography of the rural American South. Selected individual and group shows are displayed across six to eight nontraditional venues around the Courthouse Square in Zebulon, Georgia, during the festival weekend September 18–20, 2026. Up to 5 images. Juror Jerry Atnip. — Deadline: June 28, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Overcoming · Decagon Gallery
item.description: Online juried photography exhibition on the theme "What Remains Standing" — survival, resilience, and endurance after hardship, including personal loss, illness, grief, and displacement. Selected work is shown in a curated online exhibition with published catalog, social and newsletter promotion, certificate of participation, and digital badge; first place also receives a solo webpage exhibition. Juried by photographer and Vision Quest Workshops founder Douglas Beasley. Online exhibition runs August 20 – October 20, 2026. Open to photographers worldwide, all experience levels. $1,000 total cash awards. — Deadline: August 3, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $500 / $250 / $150 + HMs.

item.title: Through The Lens 2026
item.description: Online juried photography exhibition from the Marin Society of Artists, a long-running California artist organization. Open to all styles of photography, all subjects, and all types of photographic manipulation. Juried by Susan Spiritus, a fine-art photography gallerist and curator with over 50 years in the field. Selected work is presented in an online virtual gallery and YouTube showcase, July 26 – September 26, 2026, with a virtual reception on August 2. Cash awards: $500 first, $300 second, $100 third, plus honorable mentions. — Deadline: July 12, 2026. Fee: $30–$35. Prize: $500 / $300 / $100.

item.title: Midwest Center for Photography Juried Exhibition 2027
item.description: Annual international subject-matter photography competition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas, judged on the merit of individual images across five categories: Architecture, Close-Up, Landscape, Portrait, and Street Photography. Selected work is shown in the gallery March 5–21, 2027 and given online and gallery representation. Awards include $500 in Director's Choice Awards plus $100 for each of the five categories, with People's Choice Honorable Mentions in each category. Open to all photographers internationally. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: $50/5 images. Prize: $500 Director's Choice + $100 per category.

item.title: Queer|Art|Mentorship 2027 · Queer|Art
item.description: Year-long mentorship pairing early-career LGBTQIA+ artists one-on-one with an established queer mentor in their field, across Film, Literature, Performance, and Visual Art (photography falls under Visual Art). The 10-month program (January–October 2027) includes a $2,500 stipend, travel funding for a spring retreat, one-on-one coaching from staff, professional networking outreach, and access to the Queer|Art alumni network. Open to self-identified queer, lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, non-binary, and/or intersex artists based in the United States who are early-career with an existing body of work, not currently enrolled in school, and have a specific project to develop. Two-stage application: Part One via Google Form due June 15, 2026; invited applicants complete a detailed SlideRoom submission by July 31. Fellows selected by mentors in September; acceptances announced mid-October 2026. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $2,500 stipend + mentorship.

item.title: Exposure: Identity and the Evolving Image · Global Village Museum of Arts and Cultures
item.description: International juried photography exhibition at the Global Village Museum of Arts and Cultures in Fort Collins, Colorado, inviting photographers to explore identity through self-portraiture and photographic imagery — asking how we see ourselves and what it means to be seen. The brief connects contemporary photographic practice with the medium's technical and cultural history, including the legacy of Kodak in Northern Colorado. Open to photographers 18+ worldwide; work must have been created between 2016 and 2026. Selected works are exhibited and professionally printed at 16×20 inches. Exhibition runs October 2, 2026 – January 22, 2027. — Deadline: August 28, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Museum exhibition + professional printing.

item.title: International Small Works Photography Competition and Exhibition · Robert Anderson Gallery
item.description: International juried competition at the Robert Anderson Gallery in Denver, Colorado, celebrating the intimacy of small photographic images — work whose longest dimension, including frame, does not exceed 15 inches. Open to photographers worldwide aged 18+, with no restriction on subject matter or technique; digital, film, alternative, and mixed-media work where photography is central are all eligible. Juried by photographer Wendi Schneider and master printer Ron Landucci. Exhibition October 2 – December 22, 2026. — Deadline: August 2, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: $500 Best in Show + 3 × $200 merit + exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Emerging Vision: CPAC Biennial Student Show · Colorado Photographic Arts Center
item.description: Biennial juried student exhibition at the Colorado Photographic Arts Center (CPAC) in Denver, open internationally to current undergraduate and graduate students enrolled at a post-secondary institution who are not graduating before the end of the 2025–2026 academic year. All lens-based media eligible. Juried by Laura Sackett, creative director and co-founder of LensCulture. Best in Show receives a feature article on LensCulture.com, promotion in its newsletter (580,000+ subscribers), $150 custom printing from Digital Silver Imaging, and CPAC membership; Honorable Mention receives printing and membership. Exhibition November 20, 2026 – January 2, 2027. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Photography of Place · Robert A. Peck Gallery
item.description: International juried photography exhibition at the Robert A. Peck Gallery, a 6,000-square-foot teaching gallery at Central Wyoming College in Riverton. The call seeks images shot in Wyoming that capture unexpected aspects of the state with innovation, aesthetic finesse, and thought-provoking narrative — explicitly avoiding typical visitor-guide imagery. Open to artists worldwide; all photographic formats accepted. There is no entry fee and the gallery takes no commission on sales, fully insuring exhibited work. Juried by Lonnie Slack, Nita Kehoe, and George Kahrl. $10,000 in awards. Exhibition September 11 – October 16, 2026. — Deadline: August 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000 in awards + exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Honeywell Photography Competition · Honeywell Arts & Entertainment
item.description: Juried photography competition and exhibition at the Clark Gallery in the Honeywell Center, Wabash, Indiana. Open to U.S. residents of all ages — amateurs, professionals, and students — in three categories: Color, Black & White (including sepia), and Altered Images. Artwork must be original and completed within five years of the deadline, and ready to hang. Jurors are not announced in advance to protect the integrity of the show. Awards include Best of Show plus first, second, and third place in each category and ten honorable mentions. Exhibition August 18 – September 23, 2026. — Deadline: July 11, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $200 Best of Show + exhibition.

item.title: Snapped-2026: Art Bias Photography Open
item.description: International juried photography exhibition at Art Bias Studio 114, an artists' collective gallery in San Carlos, California. Four individually juried categories: Black & White, Color, Film Captured, and Youth (18 and under). Open to photographers worldwide who own copyright to their work; note that selected prints must be hand-delivered to the gallery (no shipping or receiving available). Juried by Natalie Saprykina (art advisor, founder of White on White Gallery) and Michael Endicott (Bay Area photographer, former Edge of Frame Gallery director). Cash awards of $100, $75, and $50 for first, second, and third in each category, plus honorable mentions. Exhibition August 2 – 27, 2026. — Deadline: June 29, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $100 / $75 / $50 per category + exhibition.

item.title: La Napoule Art Foundation — International Artist Residency Spring 2027
item.description: One-month international artist residency at a historic château on the French Riviera, overlooking the Mediterranean Sea. Open to emerging and established artists of all disciplines including photography, aged 18+, with no limitation on nationality. Residents receive accommodations in the château, a private studio workspace, daily breakfast, and most evening meals. Participants must communicate effectively in English or French. Residency dates March 2 – 30, 2027. Applications are evaluated on artistic vision, professional commitment, work quality, project significance, and collaborative willingness. Artists may apply once per calendar year; previous recipients may reapply but are given lower priority. Note: the historic château is not handicapped accessible. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency.

item.title: AAP Magazine #59 Shapes · All About Photo
item.description: Shapes-themed issue of AAP Magazine. Open to photographers 18+; submit a cohesive series of at least 3 images (up to 40) exploring geometric and organic forms across any genre — architecture, portrait, landscape, street or experimental. 25 winners published in AAP Magazine Volume 59 with online gallery placement and a free copy. Cash prizes: $500 (1st), $300 (2nd), $200 (3rd). Early-bird fee ($30 for first 3 images, $5 each additional) ends June 19, 2026; regular fee $35 thereafter. — Deadline: July 7, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $1,000 + publication.

item.title: Commonwealth Youth Photography Competition 2026 · Royal Commonwealth Society
item.description: Annual free competition for young photographers aged 18–30 who are citizens or residents of a Commonwealth nation. The 2026 theme, 'Waves of Change', invites images of oceans and waterways — their majesty, their vulnerability, and the communities whose lives depend on them — and of environments and communities in flux. One overall winner receives £1,000; three category winners each receive £250. Winners and finalists gain international recognition, with selected entries showcased at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) 2026 in Antigua and Barbuda. — Deadline: June 22, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £1,000 + £250 ×3.

item.title: Emerging Artists 2027 · Fotografiska Tallinn
item.description: Open call from Fotografiska Tallinn's regional Emerging Artists platform for early-career photographers from the Baltics (Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania) and Finland. Selected artists are shown in a group exhibition at Fotografiska Tallinn in autumn 2027 and receive personalised mentorship, engagement with field experts, visibility through Fotografiska's communication channels, and a place in the museum's public programming and workshops. Selection is made by an international jury. Open to photographers of all ages at an early stage of their creative journey or whose work has not yet gained wider regional recognition. — Deadline: October 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Group exhibition + mentorship.

item.title: In The Practice of Seeing — National Juried Photography Exhibition · Jacksonville State University
item.description: National juried photography exhibition at Jacksonville State University's Hammond Gallery in Alabama, open to photographers working in all photographic processes — digital, film, alternative processes, mixed media incorporating photography, and photographic installations. The brief frames photography as an active process of perception rather than mere representation. Selected works are shown in the Manners Gallery, August 27–September 24, 2026. Juried by Jim Reiman, Assistant Professor of Photography and Graphic Design at Valdosta State University. Cash awards: $500 first, $300 second, $100 third. — Deadline: July 6, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: $500 / $300 / $100 + exhibition.

item.title: No-Type Issue No. 03 — America
item.description: Themed open call from No-Type, an independent Chicago photography publisher, for the third issue of its magazine. Guided by Langston Hughes' poem "Let America Be America Again," the issue invites photographs exploring American identity and life — community, joy, and resilience as well as inequality and social challenge — and what America is, has been, and might become. Guest-edited by Chicago-based photographer Kenn Cook Jr. Selected photographers announced September 15, 2026; high-resolution files due September 22. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Women United Art Magazine — Issue XIV
item.description: International juried magazine spotlighting women artists across all visual disciplines, including photography. Selected artists are featured in the Summer 2026 Issue XIV with social media promotion and a complimentary digital copy. The sliding-scale entry fee (symbolic €10 / reduced €25 / standard €35) lets artists choose what reflects their circumstances; those from countries affected by conflict, disaster, or the suppression of women's rights can request a fee waiver. Submit up to four works of recent or best work. — Deadline: June 10, 2026. Fee: €10–€35. Prize: Publication.

item.title: i can't get at the poem of this · midwest nice art
item.description: Juried virtual exhibition welcoming all visual and performance mediums — including photography, sculpture, fiber, installation, video, sound, painting, and works on paper. The brief, drawn from a line in Alice Notley's poetry, invites artists to share the poetry or story behind a piece — what they were thinking about while making the work. Juried by Angela Zonunpari, an artist-editor-writer based in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. Online exhibition on view from August 15, 2026. Open to artists worldwide. — Deadline: July 20, 2026. Fee: $5. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Vision & Expression: The Art of Photography · PH21 Gallery
item.description: Curated international group photography exhibition exploring photography as an expressive fine-art practice in the twenty-first century — portraiture, landscape, still life, staged, abstract, and conceptual work all welcome. Curated by Zsolt Bátori (PhD; founder/director PH21 Gallery; Photolucida board member) and Borbála Jász (art historian; Photolucida juror). Curator's Choice receives three free entries for future PH21 themed calls; honorable mentions also recognized. Discounted rates (€15–20) for students, unwaged, and low-income economies. Early bird deadline July 13, final July 20. Exhibition at PH21 Gallery in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter, September 19 – October 13, 2026. AI-generated photo-based images welcome if clearly labelled. — Deadline: July 20, 2026. Fee: €25–€50. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Memory: What Remains · TCG Gallery
item.description: International open call exploring memory in all its dimensions — personal, collective, cultural, historical, and imagined — through traces of the past, family histories, identity, loss, nostalgia, landscapes, and archives. Open to all photographic genres, processes, and mixed media. Blind jury process; approximately 35 images selected. Online exhibition August 1 – September 1, 2026. Fee waivers available on request. — Deadline: July 25, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Space Between Us · Decagon Gallery
item.description: Free online photography exhibition exploring the emotional residue of human connection — the invisible architecture that feelings leave behind through atmosphere, absence, intimacy, silence, longing, routine, emotional distance, and memory. Curated and juried by the Decagon Gallery team. Selected work appears in a curated online exhibition with catalog, a dedicated exhibition page, an Instagram feature, and individual curatorial reflections responding to each submission. Exhibition August 15 – October 15, 2026. Open to photographers worldwide; all styles and processes welcome. — Deadline: July 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Abandoned · A Photographer's Place
item.description: Themed call exploring abandonment — physical, emotional, environmental, social, or symbolic — through images of absence, decay, isolation, memory, transition, and what remains. Both traditional and experimental photographic processes welcome. Juror: Marty Evans. Exhibition July 8–31, 2026 at A Photographer's Place in Raleigh, NC, with an opening reception July 10, 7–9 PM. Selected artists may optionally have work printed in-house on the gallery's Canon ImagePROGRAF Pro-1100. — Deadline: June 22, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Cut+Paste Magazine Issue 18 — Timeless
item.description: Winter 2026 issue of indie photography publication Cut+Paste, themed Timeless — elements and motifs that could belong to any century, with timeless winter landscapes and interiors in a neutral and blue palette. Accepts portraits, nature, still life, and macro photography. No nudity, profanity, or AI art. Pays $15 base plus $5–10 per additional piece if selected. — Deadline: July 5, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication + payment.

item.title: Prix de Photographie Marc Ladreit de Lacharrière 2026 · Académie des beaux-arts
item.description: 16th edition of the biennial photography project grant created by the Académie des beaux-arts at the initiative of Marc Ladreit de Lacharrière. A €30,000 bursary lets a confirmed photographer carry out an ambitious original project in complete freedom of theme and approach over a two-year working period, culminating in an exhibition at the Pavillon Comtesse de Caen, Institut de France in Paris. Open internationally with no age limit. Applications are made online via the Académie's dedicated platform. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €30,000.

item.title: Summer Open 2026 · Gallery PHOTIQ
item.description: Open-theme juried photography exhibition at Gallery PHOTIQ, a fine-art photography gallery in Royal Leamington Spa. Selected works are printed, mounted and framed at no cost to the artist, with a percentage of any sales paid to the photographer. The Curator's Award may lead to a solo exhibition. — Deadline: June 21, 2026. Fee: From £10. Prize: £100 / £50 + possible solo show.

item.title: Viewpoint Photographic Art Center — 2027 Call for Exhibit Proposals
item.description: Sacramento non-profit photography center seeking proposals for solo and group exhibitions running January–December 2027. Main Gallery proposals are open to all artists working in the photographic arts; the more intimate Step-Up Gallery is reserved for current Viewpoint members. Exhibits run roughly four weeks in both galleries. Submit a cohesive body of work — a representative selection of 20 images plus a short artist statement — reviewed by the Viewpoint Curatorial Committee. Maximum two proposals per artist; past solo exhibitors must wait three years before another solo show. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: Fabula Works — Cycle(s)
item.description: Second open call from Rome curatorial platform Fabula Works, themed Cycle(s). Two photographers are selected for a fall exhibition at Millepiani in Rome (November 6 – December 22, 2026), with printing and exhibition promotion fully covered. All genres welcome; the jury seeks work that moves beyond familiar aesthetics with a distinct perspective. Guest juror is photographer Carolyn Mendelsohn (Nikon Europe Ambassador). Submit 10–25 photographs as a portfolio with biography and artist statement. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: €25. Prize: Exhibition (production covered).

item.title: Still, Life · Photobook Cafe & Rapid Eye Darkroom
item.description: Quarterly open call from Photobook Cafe and Rapid Eye Darkrooms, themed Still, Life — exploring the tension between motion and pause, presence and aftermath, with guest judge Elliott Gunn. Open to amateur, emerging, and established photographers worldwide. 35 selected photographers are featured in a group exhibition and printed zine at The Photobook Cafe in London. Three Best in Show winners receive a complimentary group exhibition. Exhibition opening July 30, 2026. — Deadline: July 20, 2026. Fee: £25. Prize: Exhibition + zine publication.

item.title: Close-up Photographer of the Year 2026 (CUPOTY 8)
item.description: The 8th edition of CUPOTY, the international competition dedicated to close-up, macro, and micro photography. Eleven categories cover Animals, Insects, Invertebrate Portrait, Arachnids, Butterflies & Dragonflies, Underwater, Plants, Fungi & Slime Moulds, Intimate Landscape, Studio Art, and Young CUPOTY (under 18). The overall winner receives £2,500 plus a macro kit and trophy; category winners receive £250 each. Earlybird pricing runs to June 7; entries accepted up to a week after the July 12 deadline. — Deadline: July 12, 2026. Fee: £22 / £33 / £44 (6 / 15 / 30 images). Prize: £2,500 + macro kit; £250 per category.

item.title: Self — Carlotta Gallery
item.description: Carlotta Gallery's themed virtual exhibition on self-portraiture — a practice as old as photography itself. The call welcomes portraits that examine how one appears and how one is momentarily held by the camera, from literal self-portraits to conceptual approaches to identity and presence. Free to apply, pay only if selected; selected work is shown in a virtual exhibition for 6–12 months with catalogue, Collections-page listing, and certificate. — Deadline: July 10, 2026. Fee: Free (£20–£35 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Colours III — Carlotta Gallery
item.description: The third edition of Carlotta Gallery's themed virtual exhibition celebrating colour — work that engages with colour in bold, unexpected, and original ways, from saturated compositions to subtle tonal variations. Free to apply, pay only if selected; selected work is shown in a virtual exhibition for 6–12 months with catalogue, permanent Collections-page listing, and certificate. — Deadline: July 20, 2026. Fee: Free (£20–£35 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Intentional Unconventional — Experimental Photography & Video · Photo Cleveland
item.description: Photo Cleveland's avant-garde multimedia exhibition for work that breaks from conventional imagery and storytelling, favoring abstraction, non-linear structures, and unconventional techniques. The focus is on how an image was made rather than its subject — work where the artist pushed beyond traditional methods. Accepts photography, video, and mixed media (mixed media must have photography as its main component). Selected works are shown in a physical exhibition at The Brownhoist in Cleveland, opening Saturday July 11 (6–9 PM, with a live audio-visual installation by Ryan Kinney and Jim Szudy) and running July 11–31, 2026. No nudity (all-ages event); no religious or political themes. Artists may submit up to three works. — Deadline: June 27, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 works) / $20 (2 videos). Prize: Group exhibition at The Brownhoist.

item.title: New South, Volume III · Atlanta Center for Photography
item.description: Open call for the Atlanta Center for Photography's 2026 group publication, New South, Volume III — a self-published photo book featuring lens-based work made in, of, from, and about the American South. The 2025 edition featured over 81 artists. ACP frames the South broadly: defined by relationship and impact rather than personal Southern heritage, location, or 'quintessentially Southern' imagery. Open to emerging and established photographers; ACP especially encourages submissions from those who identify as Black, Indigenous, Latinx, Asian, LGBTQ+, and people with disabilities. Submit 1–5 images. Selected works appear in a high-quality 8x10 printed book (60 to 100+ pages), produced and sold through the ACP website, approved retailers, and in person in Atlanta by early October 2026. — Deadline: June 14, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Space to Feel — SaveArtSpace Bus Shelter Exhibition
item.description: Public art exhibition on bus shelter advertising space in Miami, FL, curated by Leah Guzman, a board-certified art therapist and professional artist. The theme explores emotional honesty, tenderness, healing, and human connection — celebrating vulnerability and mental health through art. Open to all mediums, including photography, and to artists of all ages and backgrounds. Selected works are displayed on Miami bus shelters for at least one month starting August 14, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has run public art billboard and transit exhibitions since 2015; fees are structured as tax-deductible donations supporting exhibition production. — Deadline: June 29, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Bus shelter exhibition in Miami.

item.title: Ode to Womanhood — SaveArtSpace Billboard Exhibition
item.description: Public art exhibition on billboard and bus shelter advertising space throughout New York City, curated by Ceres (Diaja), an award-winning photographer. The theme celebrates womanhood in all its authenticity, with emphasis on counterculture perspectives that challenge societal expectations around aging, career, marriage, and motherhood. Open to all mediums, including photography, and to artists of all ages and backgrounds. Selected works are displayed across NYC for at least one month starting August 7, 2026; artists are notified after July 6, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has run public art exhibitions since 2015; fees are tax-deductible donations supporting production. — Deadline: June 22, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Billboard exhibition in NYC.

item.title: Home Is Where I Make It — SaveArtSpace Billboard Exhibition
item.description: Public art exhibition on billboard advertising space in New York City. The theme explores the experiences of making homes in unfamiliar places — celebrating how immigrants and their children build new rituals and communities. Open to artists of all ages and backgrounds; photography welcome. Selected works are displayed on NYC billboards for at least one month starting July 24, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has run public art billboard exhibitions since 2015; fees are structured as tax-deductible donations supporting exhibition production. — Deadline: June 8, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Billboard exhibition in NYC.

item.title: The Open Road: Endless Horizons · International Photography Hall of Fame
item.description: International photography competition from the International Photography Hall of Fame and Museum (IPHF) marking the 100th anniversary of Route 66. Photographers worldwide are invited to reflect on the spirit of the open road — wanderlust, resilience, and discovery — in their own environments. Selected works are featured in an online exhibition at iphf.org. Awards: Grand Prize $1,000, First Place $500, Second Place $250, Third Place $100. Jurors: Susan Hacker Stang (photographer/educator), Shellee Graham (photographer and Route 66 ambassador), and Jim Ross (Route 66 historian). Open internationally to artists 18+; work must be original and not previously exhibited at IPHF. AI-generated or significantly AI-altered work is not eligible. — Deadline: June 21, 2026. Fee: Free members / $35 non-members. Prize: $1,000 grand prize + exhibition.

item.title: forgotten · A Smith Gallery
item.description: Online juried exhibition exploring the forgotten — abandoned, buried, erased, lost, repressed, bygone, neglected, vanished. Juror Ann Mitchell, a Southern California artist, curator, and educator (BFA Art Center College of Design, MFA Claremont Graduate University) whose work explores landscape, memory, and transformation. Up to 47 images selected; 27 featured in the hardbound "The 27" exhibition book. Awards: Juror's Award (online solo exhibition, book, blog feature), Directors' Award (book, blog feature), Visitors' Award ($100 for most Instagram likes). Exhibition July 31 – September 10, 2026 online, with reception August 29 at 3pm CST. — Deadline: July 6, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Personality: The Face and Its Absence · PH21 Gallery
item.description: Curated international group photography exhibition exploring personality and portraiture beyond the traditional face — through the body, objects, spaces, traces, absence, or symbolic associations. All creative photographic interpretations welcome, including AI-generated photo-based images. Curated by Zsolt Bátori (PhD; founder/director PH21 Gallery; Photolucida board member) and Borbála Jász (art historian; Photolucida juror). Curator's choice receives three free entries for future PH21 exhibitions; honorable mentions also recognized. Special rate for students, unwaged, and low-income economies (€15–20). Early bird deadline June 15 at reduced rates; final deadline June 22. Exhibition at PH21 Gallery in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter, August 22 – September 15, 2026. — Deadline: June 22, 2026. Fee: €25–€50. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: DECAY, CORROSION, RUST · New York Center for Photographic Arts
item.description: Themed juried call for photography of decay, corrosion, and rust — abandoned buildings, rusted vehicles, peeling paint, junkyards — in any photographic medium. Cash prizes total $4,000 across ten awards: $1,100 Grand Prize, three First Prizes of $400, three Second Prizes of $325, three Third Prizes of $250, plus 20 Juror Selections and 20 Honorable Mentions. Juried by Darren Ching, co-owner of Klompching Gallery, New York. Winners featured in the NYC4PA online gallery and catalog with certificates; the winning image appears on the NYC4PA homepage. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers; 2-D work only. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: $4,000.

item.title: 2026 Portrait Award · The Independent Photographer
item.description: The Independent Photographer's monthly themed competition cycle, this round dedicated to portrait photography. Total prize pool $2,700: 1st prize $1,000, 2nd $600, 3rd $400, plus seven $100 finalist prizes. Winners exhibited in London and featured to the platform's 970k+ Instagram following. All entrants receive a free online portfolio. Judge: Luisa Dörr, the Brazilian photographer known for her portrait work. Submissions are tiered: $15 for 1 image, $30 for 3, $45 for 6.
